slice_goal: Inspect exactly one operator-maintained Internet Archive/Wayback developer artifact that addresses automated-access request/data limits or rate policy for the pending hosted-durability quota gate.

candidate.classification: same pending hosted Wayback/CDX access mechanism; this slice adds operator-maintained data-limit evidence rather than a new mechanism identity

observations: The README states that the CDX server is deployed as part of the web.archive.org Wayback Machine and responds to HTTP GET queries.
For large or bulk queries it recommends the Pagination API.

Its Query Result Limits section states that the server configuration has an absolute maximum length for one query, currently documented as 150000 by default, and supports positive/negative limit values.
It states that offset-based pagination does not scale well for large queries because the server rereads/skips from the beginning.
Its Resumption Key section provides showResumeKey/resumeKey for efficiently splitting a larger query into smaller queries when a query limit or maximum query limit is reached.
The inspected artifact does not state a request-per-second, request-per-window, monthly, trial or paid quota policy for public web.archive.org automated access.

The inspected artifact does not state an availability, retention or durability SLA for the hosted service, and does not prove that the exact automated route remains usable when every optional finite quota is zero.

comparison.data_limit_policy: partially_proven: a per-query result ceiling/configurable maximum and resumable pagination are documented
comparison.request_rate_policy: not_proven: no request-rate/window policy in the inspected artifact
comparison.zero_incremental_monetary_cost: not_proven_by_this artifact for exact automated entitlement; prior role-local general-access evidence is insufficient to close the exact automated route
comparison.hosted_durability: not_proven: no SLA/retention guarantee in the inspected artifact
comparison.residual_work_or_protected_or_manual_use: not shown as required by this source, but absence is not sufficient to accept the hosted route because quota/durability gates remain open
